name: Minnesota
phones_sentence: County veterans service office phones and hours come from the Minnesota Association of County Veterans Service Officers; street addresses come from the officers’ pages or the state Attorney General’s handbook. Call before you go.

offices.source_title: Minnesota Association of County Veterans Service Officers: Find a CVSO
offices.note: County Veterans Service Officers can help with VA claims, pension and survivor benefits and Minnesota state benefits at no charge. Call the office first; hours vary and some counties are open only part of the week.

programs.name: Minnesota veterans: accredited claims help
programs.organization: Minnesota Department of Veterans Affairs and County Veterans Service Offices
programs.description: Free help from your County Veterans Service Officer and the Minnesota Department of Veterans Affairs with VA claims, appeals, pension and survivor benefits, plus state benefits. Every Minnesota county has a veterans service office.
programs.next_step: Choose your county for its Veterans Service Office, or call MDVA’s one-stop line, 1-888-LinkVet (888-546-5838), seven days a week. For a state claims officer, the St. Paul Claims Office is 612-970-5662 and the Fargo Claims Office, which assists northwest Minnesota, is 701-451-4640.
constraints: Hours differ by office; some counties are open only part of the week, so call first.
Minnesota has Tribal Veterans Service Officers, listed by the state department; they are not shown on county cards.

programs.name: Minnesota Aging Pathways (formerly the Senior LinkAge Line)
programs.description: Minnesota’s free statewide aging line, run by the Board on Aging with the area agencies on aging. It is the state’s long-term care options counseling service and its Aging and Disability Resource Center for older adults, and it helps with housing, transportation, meals, in-home help and Medicare. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Call 800-333-2433, Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., or choose a county above for its area agency on aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

programs.name: Medicare counseling (SHIP) for Minnesota
programs.organization: Minnesota Board on Aging, Minnesota Aging Pathways
programs.description: Free, unbiased help with Medicare choices, enrollment and costs. Minnesota Aging Pathways is the state’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP).
programs.next_step: Call 800-333-2433, Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: The line is a telephone and chat service; for a plan decision, have your Medicare card and your drug list ready.

programs.name: Minnesota Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
programs.organization: Minnesota Board on Aging, Office of Ombudsman for Long-Term Care
programs.description: Statewide advocacy for people in nursing homes, boarding care homes, assisted living, customized living, foster care and home care, delivered by regional ombudsmen and, in some places, certified volunteers.
programs.next_step: Call 800-657-3591 (toll-free) or 651-431-2555, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, and give the county and facility name. To report suspected abuse, neglect or financial exploitation of a vulnerable adult, call the Minnesota Adult Abuse Reporting Center at 844-880-1574, 24 hours a day. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency.

programs.name: Free legal help for Minnesota veterans
programs.organization: Minnesota Assistance Council for Veterans (Vetlaw); LawHelpMN
programs.description: The Minnesota Assistance Council for Veterans’ Vetlaw program gives Minnesota veterans free legal information, referrals and advice on most legal topics and holds legal clinics across the state. LawHelpMN.org explains civil legal issues and helps you find your local legal aid program.
programs.next_step: Call Vetlaw at 651-200-4750 or email vetlaw@mac-v.org to schedule time with a staff attorney, or ask about the next clinic near you.
constraints: Vetlaw attorneys advise on Minnesota state law only, not federal law or other states’ law.
Most free veteran legal aid programs screen by income, case type and location; Vetlaw will help you see which you qualify for.

programs.name: VA health care systems serving Minnesota
programs.description: Minnesota veterans are served mainly by the Minneapolis VA Health Care System (medical center at One Veterans Drive, Minneapolis, 612-725-2000, with 15 locations in Minnesota and western Wisconsin) and the St. Cloud VA Health Care System (medical center at 4801 Veterans Drive, 320-252-1670, with clinics in Brainerd, Alexandria and Montevideo). The association’s health care page also names Sioux Falls among the medical centers Minnesota veterans can use.
programs.next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic and its medical center. Not enrolled yet? Ask your county veterans service officer for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves a county depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.

coverage_scope: Referral edition. All 87 counties have a county veterans service office, an Area Agency on Aging and the state long-term care ombudsman line. The ombudsman office publishes one statewide line, so every county shows it. Eight independent living centers are shown for the counties each lists; five west-central counties are not named by any center in the national directory.
coverage_note: County veterans service office phones and hours come from the Minnesota Association of County Veterans Service Officers directory, read as search excerpts; street addresses come from the officers’ pages or, where those did not show one, the state Attorney General’s undated veterans handbook. Area Agencies on Aging come from the Minnesota Board on Aging. The long-term care ombudsman line comes from the Office of Ombudsman for Long-Term Care. Independent Living Centers come from the ILRU national directory. Reviewed November 15, 2026. Contacts are not telephone-confirmed.
